The Siemens-Martin is picky by birth: §csuperheated steam only§r — plain steam cannot even get in the door. Preheat is its hungriest hour; past the line the appetite settles, and the hotter it burns, the thriftier it drinks. It also demands §3air§r — check the gas line before this furnace starts work.

The hotter the hearth, the harder recipe times get shaved — capped at half; parallelism grows with it, and the better you feed it, the more steel pours out.

Chapter B's compressor gate was built for exactly this fire-tiger.

§3Steel by the ton begins with taming the beast.§r
